name: Chirp scratch
lesson:
## Close as the push ends, open as the pull starts

Baby-scratch strokes on every eighth. The crossfader opens at the very start of the forward stroke and closes as the stroke ends; it opens again at the start of the back stroke and closes as that ends. Two fader moves per stroke, sixteen per bar.

The chirp is what happens when the fader cuts off the tail of each stroke: each direction becomes a short bird-like note. The timing that makes it a chirp is the close, which has to happen while the platter is still moving; close after the stroke stops and it is just a baby scratch with a fader. Sharp curve, fader hand light.
